about.title: Colma Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Colma is a small city, but its cemeteries, retail strips along El Camino Real, and businesses near Hillside Boulevard and Junipero Serra Boulevard see steady foot traffic year-round. When a wet floor, broken step, uneven pavement, or poorly lit walkway causes a fall, the property owner isn't automatically responsible — California law requires showing they knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn visitors in time. That's why documentation matters so much: photos of the hazard, the condition of the lighting or flooring, and any store or building surveillance footage before it's overwritten. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself; we're a free connection service that puts you in touch with an independent attorney in our network who can evaluate what happened, explain your options, and work on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. If a fall in Colma left you injured, it costs nothing to start that conversation.

whyChoose.title: Why This Matters in a Premises Case

items.title: Proving Notice Takes Evidence
items.desc: Because California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard, early photos, incident reports, and witness statements can make a real difference.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many stores and property managers overwrite security video within days or weeks, so requesting preservation of footage quickly is often critical to a claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, even if you're partly responsible for the fall, you may still recover a reduced amount rather than nothing at all.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Colma?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, the deadline is much shorter and requires an earlier claim to be filed. An attorney can help you sort out which timeline applies to your situation.

items.question: What if I fell on property near Hillside Boulevard or El Camino Real?
items.answer: Location doesn't change the legal standard, but it can affect who owns or maintains the property, which matters for figuring out who's responsible. Whether it's a retail lot, a walkway, or a shared parking area along those corridors, an attorney can help identify the right party to pursue.

items.question: Do I need proof the owner knew about the hazard?
items.answer: Yes, California law requires showing the owner knew or reasonably should have known about the dangerous condition and failed to address it. This is often established through maintenance records, prior complaints, or how long the hazard existed. That's part of why documenting the scene right after a fall is so valuable.
